---
title: "HDF5 format"
---

lfpack ≥ 1.0 writes **format 2** (`meta.attrs["format_version"] == 2`). Format 1 is read
only; see [below](#format-1).

```
<file>.h5
└─ <recording>/                 # e.g. a probe-insertion UUID
   ├─ saturation                # (n_intervals, 2) int64 [start, stop], raw LFP samples
   └─ <scale>/                  # "00" = full resolution
      ├─ meta                   # attributes, plus optional sync_samples / sync_times
      └─ codec/
         ├─ chunk_table         # (n_chunks,) one row per 8 s chunk
         ├─ basis               # (nc, m) float32, shared spatial basis
         ├─ u_values            # (Σ m·rank_j,) float16, spatial coefficients C_j
         ├─ u_norms             # (Σ rank_j,) float32, column norms of C_j
         ├─ vh_deltas           # (Σ n_kept_j,) uint16 (uint32 if needed), index deltas
         └─ vh_values           # (Σ n_kept_j,) float32, kept wavelet-packet coefficients
```

The flat datasets are gzip + shuffle compressed in 16384-element storage chunks. Chunk `j`
occupies the slice given by the cumulative sums of `m·rank`, `rank` and `n_kept` over the
table rows before it, so one read touches one or two storage chunks per dataset.

## Decoding chunk `j`

```python
U_scaled = basis @ C_j.reshape(m, rank_j) * u_norms_j   # (nc, rank_j)
flat = np.cumsum(vh_deltas_j)                           # deltas restart at every chunk
Vh_hat = np.zeros((rank_j, vh_cols_j)); Vh_hat.flat[flat] = vh_values_j
X_j = U_scaled @ inverse_wavelet_packet(Vh_hat)         # db4, level 5, then trim guards
```

`LFPackReader` does this for you. The basis holds the top-m eigenvectors of
$\sum_j U_j U_j^\top / \lVert U_j \rVert_F^2$ over the chunks' `U_scaled`, so every chunk
weighs the same.

## `chunk_table` fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rank` | uint16 | SVD rank of the chunk |
| `n_kept` | uint32 | Stored wavelet-packet coefficients |
| `vh_cols` | uint32 | Wavelet-packet slots per row |
| `ns_original` | int32 | Written samples (2048 except the last chunk) |
| `ns_extended` | int32 | Samples coded, guard bands included |
| `left_overlap` | int32 | Left guard-band samples |
| `cr_svd`, `cr_wp`, `cr_total`, `rmse` | float32 | Per-chunk diagnostics of the codec, before the basis projection |

## `meta` attributes

| Attribute | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `format_version` | int | 2 |
| `nc`, `ns_total` | int | Channels, samples |
| `fs` | float | Nominal sampling rate (Hz) |
| `fs_sync`, `t0_sync` | float | Sync-corrected rate and session time of sample 0; `NaN` if unknown |
| `epsilon`, `alpha`, `basis_size` | float, float, int | Codec parameters |
| `compress_chunk`, `compress_overlap` | int | 2048 and 128 samples |
| `geometry_x`, `geometry_y` | float32 (nc,) | Channel positions (µm) |
| `labels` | int8 (nc,) | Channel quality: 0 good, 1 dead, 2 noisy, 3 outside the brain |
| `ml`, `ap`, `dv`, `atlas_id`, `acronym` | (nc,) | Optional brain locations |
| `sglx_meta` | JSON string | Original SpikeGLX metadata |

`sync_samples` / `sync_times` (float64 child datasets of `meta`, optional) are piecewise sync
knots in this scale's sample units. They are datasets rather than attributes because an
exact fit can hold tens of thousands of knots, beyond HDF5's attribute size limit.
`fs_sync` / `t0_sync` are always their least-squares affine, so code that reads only the
attributes keeps working. Write both with `lfpack.write_sync_attrs`.

## `saturation`

Written once per recording. Attributes: `fs`, `ns_total`, `n_saturated_samples`,
`saturated_fraction`, the detection parameters and `muted` (whether the spans were zeroed).

## HDF5 version

Files are written with `libver=("earliest", "v110")`, readable by any HDF5 ≥ 1.10
(h5py ≥ 3.0). Do not switch to `libver="latest"`: it follows whatever library wrote the
file and produces files that older installs fail to read with unhelpful errors.

## Format 1 {#format-1}

Written by lfpack < 1.0: one group per chunk, `<scale>/chunks/<i>/` with `U_scaled` (nc, r)
float32, `vh_indices` int32 and `vh_values` float32, and the chunk metadata as attributes.
The older flat layout (`meta` and `chunks` at the file root) is format 1 as well. Both are
read transparently, are deprecated, and convert with `lfpack.upgrade_h5`.
